extracted.intended_audience: Vietnamese and foreign organizations and individuals subject to Vietnam IP law; IP practitioners, patent applicants, rights holders, courts, customs and enforcement authorities
extracted.subtask_description: National legislation (Law No.50/2005/QH11) setting out definitions, conditions for protection, establishment of IP rights (copyrights, related rights, industrial property, plant varieties), permitted uses, terms, infringement acts and remedies (civil, administrative, criminal, border control, provisional measures) in Vietnam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects of intellectual property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: This Law stipulates copyright, copyright-related rights; industrial property rights; rights in plant varieties and for the protection of these rights. Objects of industrial property rights include inventions; industrial designs; layout-designs of semiconductor integrated circuits; business secrets; trademarks; trade names and geographical indications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates categories of protectable subject-matter (works, performances, phonograms, broadcasts; inventions, designs, marks, plant varieties, trade secrets etc.). Useful to determine which statutory regime applies to a given subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of invention (technical solution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Invention is a technical solution, in form of a product or a process, to resolve a specific problem by utilizing laws of nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the conceptual boundary of 'invention' for industrial property; used to determine if an application falls under invention protection (patent) as opposed to other IP regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial design is appearance of a product expressed in shapes, lines, dimensions, colors or any combination thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines what visual/ornamental features may be protected as an industrial design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiconductor integrated circuit and layout-design definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Semiconductor integrated circuit: a product (final or intermediate) in which elements and interconnections are integrally formed to perform an electronic function. Layout-design: a three-dimensional disposition of circuitry elements and interconnections in a semiconductor integrated circuit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies eligibility of IC products and layout-designs for industrial property protection and the meaning of 'layout-design'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark and types (including collective and certification marks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark is any sign used to distinguish goods or services of different organizations and individuals. Collective mark is used to distinguish goods or services of members from non-members. Certification mark is licensed to others to certify characteristics (origin, materials, methods, quality, safety, etc.). Associated marks are marks registered by same owner and identical or similar and used for identical/similar or inter-related goods/services. Well-known mark is a mark widely known throughout the territory of Vietnam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines trademark categories and special marks; used to assess registration eligibility, scope of protection and special treatment (e.g., well-known marks recognized by use).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade name
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade name is a designation of an organization or individual used in business to distinguish the business entity from others in the same field and area of business; the 'area of business' is the geographical area where the entity has partners, clients or reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trade name rights are tied to lawful use and geographic business area — relevant for disputes with similar business designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographical indication
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographical indication is a sign used to indicate a product originating from a specific area, locality, region or country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the category and function of GIs for registration and protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business secret (trade secret) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Business secret is information obtained from financial, intellectual, investment which is undisclosed and susceptible to application in business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection depends on lawful acquisition and secret keeping (see establishment of rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant variety and rights to plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Plant variety is a plant grouping within a single botanical taxon of the lowest known rank, uniform and stable in propagation, distinguishable by phenotype; rights to plant varieties are rights of organizations/individuals to new plant varieties created or discovered and developed by them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets biological and distinctness/stability/uniformity criteria relevant to plant variety protection and registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection title (industrial property title) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection title is a document granted by a State authority to establish industrial property rights to inventions, industrial designs, layout-designs, marks, geographical indications; and rights to plant varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies formal instrument that confers industrial property rights (i.e., grant of a patent/design/mark/PV protection title).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyrights arise on creation (basis of appearance of copyright)
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyrights shall arise at the moment when a work is created and expressed in a certain material form regardless of its content, quality, form, means, language, whether or not it has been published or registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No formal registration required for copyright to exist; fixation/material expression suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related rights arise on fixation
rubrics_metrics.description: Related rights arise at the moment when a performance, a phonogram, a broadcast program and a satellite signal carrying encrypted program is fixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fixation (recording) is the trigger for neighboring/related rights protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of industrial property rights (registration/grant/recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property rights in inventions, industrial designs, layout-designs, marks, geographical indications shall be established on the basis of the competent state authority's decision on the grant of Protection Title in accordance with registration procedures or on the recognition of international registration under international treaties; for well-known marks, ownership rights can be established on the basis of use independently from registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that patents/designs/marks generally require grant/registration, but well-known marks may be protected via use; international registrations may be recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of trade name rights by lawful use
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property rights to trade names shall be established on the basis of lawful use of the trade names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes use-based (common-law style) protection for trade names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of business secret rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property rights in business secrets shall be established on the basis of legal acquirement and secret keeping of the business secrets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection depends on (1) lawful acquisition and (2) measures to keep information secret.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of rights to new plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights to new plant varieties shall be established on the basis of the competent state authority’s decision on the grant of Plant Variety Protection Title in accordance with registration procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant variety protection requires state grant following registration procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on exercise of IP rights
rubrics_metrics.description: IP rights owners may implement their rights within the scope and term of protection; exercise of IP rights shall not infringe interests of the state, the public or legitimate rights and interests of others and shall not violate other applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights are subject to statutory limits and public interest considerations; balancing with other rights and laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: State's power to prohibit, limit or compel licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure objectives of national defense, security, people's living and other national interests, the State may prohibit or limit IP rights owners from exercising rights or compel them to license one or more of their rights subject to appropriate conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets state sovereign exception and compulsory licensing grounds (public interest, national security, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: State policies on intellectual property
rubrics_metrics.description: State shall recognize and protect IP rights while ensuring equal benefits of IP rights holders and the public interest; shall not protect IP objects contrary to social morality, public order, or harmful to national defense and security; shall encourage creation, exploitation of IP assets, provide financial assistance, and prioritize training and IP administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy objectives to interpret/guide implementation of the Law and secondary regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of works protected by copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Literary, artistic and scientific works protected include literary and scientific works, lectures, journalistic works, musical works, dramatic works, cinematographic works, fine and applied art works, photographic works, architectural works, maps/graphics, folk artistic works, computer programs and compilations of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Computer programs are explicitly protected as literary works (source or object code); compilation protection does not extend to the underlying documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality requirement for protected works
rubrics_metrics.description: Protected works must be created directly by the author's intelligence without reproducing others' works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes an originality/origin requirement for copyright protection; derivative works are protected only if they do not infringe rights in the underlying works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject matter excluded from copyright protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded: information solely for communication; legal normative documents, administrative and judicial documents and their official translations; processes, systems, methods of operation, definitions, principles and statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates ideas, procedures, facts and official legal texts from copyrightable expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal rights of authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal rights include right to name the work, to have real name/pseudonym indicated, to publish or authorize publication, and to protect integrity of the work (object to derogatory modification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral rights are recognized and include indefinite protection for certain personal rights (see terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Property (economic) rights of authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Property rights include the right to create derivative works; perform the work to the public; reproduce; circulate copies; communicate to the public by wire/wireless/electronic network; lease originals or copies of cinematographic works or computer programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic rights can be exercised by authors or assigned/exclusively owned and are subject to permission and remuneration obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses without permission and without payment (copyright exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated exceptions include: self-duplicating a single copy for personal scientific research and individual teaching; reasonable quotation without alteration for commentary or illustration; quotation for articles/periodicals/radio/TV/documentaries; copying for archives in libraries; performing works in cultural gatherings/promotional campaigns without charge; recording/reporting performances for public information/education; photographing publicly displayed fine art works for introduction; translating into Braille; importing copies for personal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions must not affect normal exploitation of the work or prejudice authors' rights; some exceptions do not apply to architectural, fine art works or computer programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use without permission but with payment (limited compulsory remuneration cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasting organizations using published works for sponsored/advertised/commercial broadcasts need not obtain permission but must pay royalties/remuneration according to Government regulation; such use must not influence normal exploitation or prejudice authors' rights; does not apply to cinematographic works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows certain mass uses subject to payment and non-prejudiciality safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of copyright protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal rights (naming, attribution, integrity) are protected indefinitely. Property rights (and some personal rights like publication) have terms: 50 years from first publication for cinematographic, photographic, dramatic, applied art works and anonymous works; otherwise life of author plus 50 years (co-authors: 50 years after last surviving co-author's death); terms end at 24:00 on 31 December of the final year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines temporal scope for economic exploitation and moral rights; special rules for anonymous works and fixation/publication timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright infringement acts (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes seizing copyrights of a work; assuming author’s name; publishing/disseminating without permission; publishing co-author's work without consent; modifying/mutilating/distorting prejudicial to honor; copying without permission (except specified exceptions); making derivative works without permission; exploiting works without paying royalties; renting without payment; photocopying/publishing/communicating via broadcast/digital devices without permission; cancelling technical protection measures; erasing/amending rights-management information; producing equipment knowing it's used to invalidate technical measures; forging author signature; exporting/importing/disseminating copies without permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List covers both traditional infringements and anti-circumvention/DRM and secondary liability related to equipment and rights-management information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of performers
rubrics_metrics.description: Performers have personal and property rights: personal rights include acknowledgment and protection of performance image; property rights include exclusive rights to fix live performance in phonograms, reproduce fixations, broadcast/communicate unfixed performances (with some exceptions), and distribute fixations to the public. Exploiters must pay remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between performers who are investors (owners) and those who are not; remuneration obligations for those who exploit performers' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of producers of phonograms
rubrics_metrics.description: Producer has exclusive rights to reproduce phonogram; distribute originals/copies by sale/rental or other technical means; and the right to get material benefits when phonogram is distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic rights for phonogram producers are analogous to copyright owners for sound recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of broadcasting organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadcasters have exclusive rights to broadcast/rebroadcast, distribute their broadcasts, fix broadcasts, and reproduce fixations; they have the right to obtain material benefits when programs are recorded, broadcast or distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protection for broadcast-originated content and associated commercial exploitation rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related rights exceptions and terms of protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Some uses of related rights do not require permission/payment (personal duplication single copy for research/teaching, reasonable quotation, temporary phonogram creation by broadcasters). Uses for commercial broadcasting or business activities require payment but not permission. Terms: performers' rights 50 years from year of fixation; producers of phonograms 50 years from publication or fixation if unpublished; broadcasters 50 years from year of broadcast; terms end at 24:00 on 31 December of final year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parallels copyright exceptions and terms but provides specific 50-year durations for related rights and defines exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related rights infringement acts (enumerated)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes abrogating rights of performers/producers/broadcasters; assuming their names; publishing/producing/communicating fixed performances/phonograms/broadcasts without permission; modifying/distorting performances prejudicial to honor; reproducing or extracting fixed performances without permission; removing/altering rights-management information; cancelling technical measures; distributing/importing when aware RMI was removed; producing equipment used to decode encrypted satellite signals; recording/disseminating continuously decoded encrypted satellite signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers direct and circumvention-related infringements of neighboring rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to request provisional measures upon/after lawsuit initiation
rubrics_metrics.description: An IP right holder may request the court to apply provisional measures if there is a threat of irreparable damage or threat of dispersal/destruction of goods suspected of infringing and relevant evidence; the court may decide to apply provisional measures at request before hearing the opinion of the party liable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables expedited protective relief (pre-trial) to preserve evidence and goods and avoid irreparable harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of provisional measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional measures applicable to suspected infringing goods and related materials include seizure; attachment; sealing/prohibition of changing status or displacing; prohibition of transferring ownership. Other measures per Civil Procedure Code may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies concrete enforcement tools available to courts to secure assets and evidence early in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations and security for requesting provisional measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requester must prove right to request and produce materials/evidence. Requester is obliged to pay compensation to the provisional measure debtor if found not to infringe and must deposit security: either 20% of value of goods subject to measures (or at least 20 million VND if goods cannot be valued) or submit a bank/credit guarantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a deterrent against abusive applications for provisional measures and secures compensation for wrongful restraints; quantifies deposit (20% or minimum VND 20 million).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and procedure for provisional measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Court shall terminate provisional measures in cases per Civil Procedure Code or if the debtor proves the measure unreasonable. Upon termination, court considers reimbursement of deposited amount; if request was unreasonable and caused damage, the requester must compensate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides due-process and remedies balancing requester and debtor interests; procedures follow Civil Procedure Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts of IPR infringement liable for administrative remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts subject to administrative remedies include infringements causing loss to consumers/society; not terminating infringement after written notice; producing/importing/transporting/trading IP counterfeit goods; producing/importing/trading articles bearing marks or GIs identical or confusingly similar to protected ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies categories of conduct typically handled administratively (fines, warnings, confiscation) as distinct from criminal liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of intellectual property counterfeit goods
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeit mark goods: goods or packaging bearing a mark/sign identical with or substantially indistinguishable from a protected mark or GI without consent. Pirated goods: copies made without consent of copyright or related rights holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiates counterfeit mark goods and pirated goods for classification and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative penalties and remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Main remedies: warning or monetary fine. Complementary remedies: confiscation of counterfeit goods/materials/implements; suspension of relevant business activities for a definite term. Restoration remedies: compelling destruction/distribution/use for non-commercial purposes (so long as it doesn't affect rights holder exploitation); delivery out of Vietnam or re-export after removal of infringing elements. Monetary fine rates at least equal to value of discovered infringing goods but not exceed five times that value; Government to detail valuation method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides range of administrative measures and sets floor/ceiling for fines relative to infringing goods' value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of preventative administrative measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Where infringement may cause serious damage to consumers/society, there is threat of dispersal or evasion, or to guarantee implementation of administrative remedies, requesters may ask competent agency to apply administrative preventative measures: temporary hold of individuals; temporary detention of goods/means/implements; search of related individuals; search of storage places; other measures per law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative counterpart to provisional judicial measures enabling immediate action to prevent evasion or destruction of evidence/goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Border control measures for IP-related imports/exports
rubrics_metrics.description: Border control measures include suspension of customs procedures for suspected infringing goods and supervision to detect goods containing signs of IP infringement. Suspension is taken at the request of the IP right holder to collect information/evidence and ensure possibility of administrative penalties or other remedies. If goods are detected as counterfeit, customs may impose administrative remedies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables IP holders to seek customs assistance to intercept suspected infringing goods at the border; ties customs action to requester obligations and deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations and security for requesting border control measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requester must prove they are the IP right holder by producing materials/evidence; provide information sufficient to identify suspected goods; lodge application and pay fees/charges; pay damages/expenses to persons subject to measures if goods found not infringing. To secure obligations, requester must deposit either 20% of value of lots subject to suspension or at least VND 20 million, or submit a bank/credit guarantee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors provisional measure security requirements; quantifies deposit and specifies documentary burdens on requester to justify customs intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures and time limits for suspension of customs procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If requester properly performs obligations, customs issues a decision to suspend procedures. Term of suspension: 10 working days from issuance; may be prolonged up to 20 working days with reasons and additional deposit. If requester fails to initiate civil lawsuit or customs does not accept administrative handling by expiration, customs shall continue completion of customs procedures and may compel requester to compensate damages and storage costs; reimburse remaining deposit after obligations paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets defined timelines and consequences for inaction by requester; protects importers from indefinite suspension and provides reimbursement/compensation mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination and supervision role of customs
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request for examination/supervision to detect goods containing signs of IP infringement, customs notifies requester when suspected lot detected; requester has three working days to request suspension of customs procedures; otherwise customs completes clearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes cooperative process and short response window for right-holders to convert supervision into suspension action.
